title: What Is Sold, Used and Published: the Se Passive

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know the *se* passive from B1 Unit 6: *se busca una persona*, *se buscan personas*. When the doer does not matter, *se* + the verb says what is done, and the verb agrees with the thing. Trade and finance are described this way all the time: what is sold, what is used, what is published.

sections.title: The se passive in Panama's economy
rows: En la zona franca se venden mercancías de muchos países.
plural thing, plural verb: goods from many countries are sold
En Panamá se usa el dólar estadounidense desde 1904.
singular thing, singular verb: the US dollar has been used since 1904
Se publicaron los Papeles de Panamá en 2016.
past tense: the Panama Papers were published in 2016
Las mercancías se reexportan a otros países.
the subject can come first: the goods are re-exported to other countries

items.spanish: En la Zona Libre de Colón se venden mercancías que luego se reexportan.
items.english: In the Colón Free Zone goods are sold which are later re-exported.

items.spanish: En Panamá se usa el dólar, y el balboa solo existe en monedas.
items.english: In Panama the dollar is used, and the balboa exists only as coins.

items.spanish: Después del escándalo se cambiaron algunas leyes.
items.english: After the scandal some laws were changed.

items.spanish: En el aeropuerto de Tocumen se conectan vuelos de todo el continente.
items.english: At Tocumen airport flights from all over the continent connect.

sections.content: Look at the thing, not at *se*: *se vende una casa*, *se venden casas*. If you want to name who did it (*fue publicado por periodistas*), the passive with *ser* + participle is the tool (you know *ser* + participle from B1 Unit 18); with *se* you leave the doer out.
